name: Siddhanath Temple, Nemawar
significance: A 10th-century sandstone Shiva temple at Nemawar built under Paramara rule, with a mandapa added about a century later. Pilgrim records cut into it are dated 1196-97 and 1223-24 CE, and it has remained in worship since.

name: Mahalingapuram Ayyappan Temple
significance: An Ayyappan temple built in 1974 in the Mahalingapuram area of Nungambakkam, Chennai, laid out in Kerala style with the eighteen steps and subsidiary shrines to Shiva, Bhagavati, Ganapathi and Subrahmanya.

name: Kootayanimoodu Chamundi Temple
significance: An 18th-century Kerala-style temple at Kootayanimoodu in Vellanad panchayat, Thiruvananthapuram district, dedicated to the goddess Chamundeswari, a fierce form of Durga.
story: The goddess is said to have been brought forth by Durga to kill the demons Chanda and Munda, and was blessed to be worshipped ever after as Chamunda.

name: Maa Markama Temple
significance: The only shrine in Odisha to the sister goddesses Markama and Karkama, at Bissam Cuttack in Rayagada district; the goddess served as tutelary deity of the Thatraja rulers, and the buffalo sacrifice once held here was discontinued in 1955.
story: Local accounts hold that Markama helped the king of Bissam Cuttack win a war by mesmerising the enemy's soldiers.

name: Mullakkal Temple
significance: A temple of nearly five hundred years standing in the centre of Alappuzha town, attributed to King Devanarayana of Chembakassery and built in old Kerala style with an open-roofed sanctum; its cracked idol was replaced with one of Rajarajeswari on 16 July 1962.
story: The goddess is said to have appeared to the king in a dream and travelled home with him, then halted at a jasmine garden where his umbrella could not be lifted, marking the spot she had chosen.

name: Cheruthazham Sree Kunninmathilakam Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Cheruthazham in Kannur district where the deity is worshipped in three aspects across the day - Dakshinamurti in the morning, Kiratamurti at noon and Umamaheshwara in the evening; the sanctum was raised by about six Brahmin families and the temple was restored from long neglect from the 1980s.
story: Legend holds that Hanuman, sent by Rama to install a lingam at Rameswaram, set down part of it here and so reached Rameswaram late.

name: Vazhappully Temple
significance: A family temple at Kazhimbram near Valapad in Thrissur district dedicated to Raja Rajeswari, noted as one of the few temples in Kerala where Gandharva is also worshipped.

name: Sree Sundareswara Temple
significance: Begun in 1908 and consecrated by Sree Narayana Guru in April 1916, this Shiva temple at Talap is one of two he consecrated to serve the Thiyya community of Malabar under British rule.

name: Sun Temple, Madkhera
significance: An east-facing Surya temple in Madkhera village, Tikamgarh district, raised under the Pratiharas and listed as a state protected monument; its sanctum holds a standing Surya on a lotus pedestal and its walls carry Dashavatara sculptures.

name: Karaikandeswarar Temple, Kanji
deity: Shiva (Karaikandeswarar), with Parvati as Periyanayagi Amman
significance: A Shiva temple at Kanji in Tiruvannamalai district, counted as the first of seven Karaikandeswarar temples strung along the banks of the Cheyyar river; its present masonry structure was put up by Se. Ve. Venkataraman Chettiar.

name: Maa Kaali & Bhagwan Shankar Temple
significance: A village temple to Kali and Shiva at Bisauri in Jaunpur district, Uttar Pradesh, administered by the Bisauri gram panchayat.

name: Nelliparampu Sreekrishna Swami Temple
significance: A Krishna temple at Nellipparambu in Kollam district, Kerala, locally reckoned to be some 1,800 years old and among the better known Vaishnava shrines of the district.

name: Kundrathur Nageswarar Temple
significance: A 12th-century Shiva temple at Kundrathur built by the Shaiva saint Sekkizhar and modelled on the Thirunageswaram temple at Kumbakonam; it is counted among the Navagraha temples associated with Rahu.

name: Sri Rajagopala Swamy Temple, Rajamadam
deity: Rajagopalaswamy (Krishna), with Sridevi, Bhudevi and Senkamalavalli Thayar
builtDisplay: built under Serfoji II of Thanjavur
significance: A Vishnu temple at Rajamadam in Thanjavur district built by the Thanjavur Maratha ruler Serfoji II, who also founded the village of Rajamadam around it.
story: The king, who had long prayed for an heir, is said to have been visited by the deity in a dream and granted a son, and raised the temple in thanks.

name: Kalika Mata Temple, New Dhrewad
significance: A Maitraka-period temple of the sandhara type, with an interior ambulatory, standing near New Dhrewad village in Devbhoomi Dwarka district; it is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as Monument of National Importance N-GJ-122.

name: Old Madiwala Someshwara Temple, Bengaluru
significance: One of the oldest temples in Bengaluru, at Madiwala, begun in the early 12th century and completed by 1247; its Tamil and Grantha inscriptions record land grants from 1247 onward and document the area under Chola and later rule.

name: Varadharajaperumal Temple, Thirubuvanai
significance: A Chola temple at Thirubuvanai in Puducherry raised by Parantaka I and carrying later inscriptions of Rajaraja Chola and Rajadhiraja I; those records show it also functioned as a teaching centre for the Vedas and other scriptures, and the building survived the French invasion of the region.

name: Thukkachi Abatsahayesvar Temple
builtDisplay: 11th c. (Rajendra Chola I); enlarged under Vikrama Chola
significance: A Chola temple on the Arasalar river at Thukkachi, east of Kumbakonam, built under Rajendra Chola I and enlarged by Vikrama Chola; its vimana resembles that of the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, and a restoration carried out between 2015 and 2023 drew UNESCO recognition.
story: Vikrama Chola, afflicted with vitiligo, is said to have been told by the deity in a dream while camped near Thukkachi to worship here for forty-eight days, after which he was cured.

name: Puttur Shree Mahalingeshwara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the town of Puttur, Dakshina Kannada district, built in Kerala style and credited to a Banga ruler; the article dates it to the 12th century while its own infobox gives the 8th.

name: Trivikrama Temple, Ter
builtDisplay: 2nd-3rd c. CE apsidal shrine; mandapa added from 6th c.
significance: An apsidal shrine at Ter in Dharashiv district regarded as the oldest standing structure in Maharashtra, built in Satavahana times to an early Buddhist caityagriha design and given a flat-roofed mandapa from about the 6th century when it passed into Hindu worship. Henry Cousens read the original building as Buddhist, a view M. S. Mate disputed in 1957.

name: Balasubramaniyaswamy Temple, Vennaimalai
significance: A hill temple to Murugan at Vennaimalai in Karur district, Tamil Nadu, run by the state Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments department and among the district's best-known visitor sites.
story: When Brahma grew proud of his role as creator, Shiva is said to have sent him to do penance at Vanjimalai, and the divine cow Kamadhenu took over creation, raising a hill of butter - vennai in Tamil - and filling the sacred tank with her milk.

name: Sun Temple, Sesai
significance: A west-facing temple to the sun god Surya in the village of Sesai, Shivpuri district, Madhya Pradesh, raised on a jagati platform.

name: Kumara Swamy Devasthana, Bengaluru
significance: A hilltop shrine to Kartikeya at Hanumanthanagar in Bengaluru, on the rise known as Mount Joy; its original panchaloha image is now kept on separate display while a later granite idol receives worship, and the shrine is likened to the Swaminatha Swamy temple in Thanjavur.

name: Prabhadevi Temple
significance: A goddess temple in Mumbai built in 1715 with funds raised by the Pathare Prabhu community to house a 12th-century image of Shakambari Devi, held to have been the family deity of the Seuna Yadava king Bimba of Devagiri; the idol was taken to Karnataka, attacked during Mughal times and finally brought to Mahim Creek before installation here.
story: Local folklore says the goddess appeared in a dream to Shyam Nayak, a devotee of the Pathare Prabhu community, who then built her a temple.

name: Thiruvullakkavu Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
deity: Dharma Sastha (Ayyappan), standing with a bow
significance: A Sastha temple at Cherpu in Thrissur district, long resorted to for Vidyarambham, the rite at which small children are initiated into letters and learning.

name: Aadi Himani Chamunda
builtDisplay: at least as old as the adjacent palace ruins of c. 1660
significance: A high mountain shrine of Chamunda Devi above Kangra in Himachal Pradesh, reckoned at least as old as the palace ruins of about 1660 beside it. Long derelict, it was restored from 1992 largely through two decades of work by the retired officer P. D. Saini, destroyed by fire in 2014 and rebuilt.
story: The goddess is said to have killed the demons Chanda and Munda by hurling great boulders down on them from the mountain top, and to take her name from them.

name: Maa Barunei Temple
deity: Barunei, a manifestation of Shakti (with Karunei)
significance: A hill shrine on Barunei Hill in Khordha district, Odisha, whose sanctum holds images of the twin goddesses Barunei and Karunei; the stream called Swarna Ganga runs from the hills beside it.

name: Maa Jhanjiri Mangala Temple
significance: A temple of the goddess Mangala, the presiding deity of Cuttack, raised by villagers and counted among the oldest in the city; a theft from it in 2015 led to the arrest of a gang.
story: A priest living in the forest is said to have seen the goddess Mangala in a dream, who asked him to build a small temple for her.

name: Ponmeri Shiva Temple
significance: A large Mahadeva temple near Vatakara in Kozhikode district commissioned by the Kadathanad kings in the 11th century, unusual for carrying a sub-shrine to Brahma, a deity seldom given one.
story: A quarrel between the ruler and his architect is said to have left the building forever unfinished, and gave Malayalam the proverb 'as incomplete as the work at Ponmeri'.

name: Ekalavya Temple
significance: A temple at Khandsa village in Gurugram, built in 1721 by a well-off villager, described as the only Hindu temple anywhere dedicated to Ekalavya of the Mahabharata.
story: Ekalavya, self-taught and found to outshine Arjuna, cut off his right thumb when Dronacharya asked for it as gurudakshina, and the temple stands where the thumb is said to have been buried.

name: Jasmalnathji Mahadev Temple, Asoda
significance: A 12th-century panchayatana Shiva temple at Asoda in Mehsana district, raised during the reign of the Chaulukya king Jayasimha Siddharaja and now a Monument of National Importance maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Chennamangalam Temple
significance: An Ayyappa temple at Chorode in Kozhikode district that also houses Shiva, Ganesha, Vishnu and Annapurneshwari; described as one of Kerala's oldest and known as a second Sabarimala, it drew large numbers when a fire kept pilgrims from Sabarimala itself.

name: Sri Gangamma Devi Temple
significance: A temple to the local goddess Gangamma in the Malleswara layout of north-western Bengaluru, given a permanent building in 2004; the annual Gangamma Jathre has been held in the locality since 1928.

name: Soundararajaperumal Temple, Thadikombu
significance: A 16th-century temple at Thadikombu in Dindigul district credited to the Vijayanagara ruler Achyuta Deva Raya, with work begun under his predecessor Aliya Rama Raya and the outer halls added in 1629 under Thirumalai Nayak; it carries rare sculpture and inscriptions from several reigns.
story: A sage cursed to live as a frog and tormented by a demon is said to have worshipped Vishnu here, who killed the demon and freed him.

name: Dudhadhari Temple
significance: A math and temple at Mathpara in Raipur founded in the 16th century by Swami Balabhadradas, who was called Dudh Ahari because he lived on milk alone and so gave the place its name. The Bhonsle Maratha ruler of Nagpur, Raghuji, later issued a charter conferring the title Rajeshri on each head of the math.

name: Aryankavu Sastha Temple
style: Dravidian, blending Kerala and Tamil traditions
significance: One of the five principal Sastha temples of Kerala, at Aryankavu in Kollam district, where the deity is worshipped as a youth seated on an elephant with Pushkala at his left and Shiva at his right; it is administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board.
story: The image is held to have been consecrated by Parashurama, and Sastha is said to have married Pushkaladevi here, an event kept each December as the Thiru Kalyanam festival.

name: Avanibhajana Pallaveshwaram Temple
significance: A Pallava cave temple cut at Seeyamangalam under Mahendravarman I in the early 7th century, among the earliest examples of rock-cut architecture in the region and holding one of the oldest surviving depictions of Nataraja; Chola and Vijayanagara additions came later.

name: Jamalapuram Temple
significance: A Venkateswara temple at Jamalapuram near Errupalem in Khammam district, described as of considerable antiquity and renovated under Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara; it is popularly called the Chinna Tirupati of Telangana.
story: The sage Jabali is said to have performed penance at a spot here called Suchi Gutta and been blessed by Venkateswara, who is worshipped as a self-manifested form.

name: Polur Temple, Kozhikode
significance: A Subrahmanya temple at Polor in Kuruvattoor panchayat, Kozhikode district, counted among the oldest in the area and connected with the Porlathiri king from whom the region takes its name; Ganapathi, Vettakkorumakan, Ayyappan and Devi are also worshipped here.
